companyDescription: AAV gene therapy developer · RGX-121/NAVSUNLI for MPS II now on FDA clinical hold with no near-term resubmission expected — but RGX-202 (Duchenne) already met its Phase III primary endpoint and BLA submission is guided for this quarter, plus a partnered retina program (ABBV-RGX-314) with positive 3-year durability data
priceNote: ⚠️ CATALYST CORRECTION: today's earlier RGNX report (also dated Sep 29, written before this refresh) used $8.62 and framed NAVSUNLI resubmission as imminent — that was wrong. Live price is $7.56 (-12.3% vs that draft). Independent research for this refresh surfaced a Aug 24, 2026 FDA clinical hold on RGX-121 that the prior draft never incorporated.
summary: ⚠️ THESIS BROKEN (catalyst pivot, not a full washout): the prior report's near-term catalyst — an imminent NAVSUNLI (RGX-121) BLA resubmission by end of Q3 2026 — is void. On Aug 24, 2026, the FDA placed a clinical hold on RGX-121 after asymptomatic spinal MRI findings (small nodules/cystic masses, characterized as nonserious/likely benign) turned up in 5 trial participants dosed 3-6 years earlier; REGENXBIO stated it 'does not expect to resubmit the RGX-121 BLA in the near term.' That specific catalyst is dead for this cycle. The real near-term catalyst is a different pipeline asset: RGX-202 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy already met its Phase III AFFINITY DUCHENNE primary endpoint with high statistical significance in Q2 2026, its confirmatory study is fully enrolled ahead of schedule, and management guided a BLA submission this quarter (Q3 2026, ending Sep 30). Analysts have largely held their ground post-clinical-hold — 11 analysts, consensus $23.73 (Strong Buy 6 / Buy 3 / Hold 2), reiterations as recent as Sep 28 (H.C. Wainwright $21) and Sep 25 (Stifel $42) — one analyst called the RGX-121 setback 'disappointing' but said 'larger catalysts remain intact,' referring to RGX-202. Cash runway >$310M pro forma into Q4 2027 reduces near-term financing risk. This is a corrected, more cautious thesis, not a dead one.

catalysts.name: ABBV-RGX-314 Wet AMD Pivotal Topline Data
catalysts.description: Partnered with AbbVie. Pivotal-trial topline data for wet AMD expected Q4 2026, alongside an actively enrolling NAAVIGATE Phase IIb/III trial in diabetic retinopathy — where REGENXBIO just reported positive 3-year durability data (Sep 24, 2026): 60% of long-term participants achieved a >2-step DRSS improvement without additional treatment.

risks: RGX-121/NAVSUNLI is not paused-and-resuming — REGENXBIO explicitly said it does NOT expect to resubmit the BLA in the near term; treat this program as impaired, not merely delayed, until new data changes that

The safety finding (spinal MRI abnormalities in dosed patients) is specific to intracisternal/intraventricular AAV dosing — investors should watch whether it raises any read-through concern for other REGENXBIO delivery routes, even though management has not flagged one
RGX-202's 'this quarter' BLA-submission guidance is company language, not an FDA-committed date — submission could slip into Q4 without formally breaking guidance

A sub-$500M market cap gene-therapy name with genuinely wide analyst target dispersion ($10-$50) — real methodology disagreement on how much of the platform's multi-asset value the market should price in after a setback

This report replaces an internally-inconsistent same-day draft that priced NAVSUNLI as imminent — a reminder that same-day 'fresh' isn't automatically accurate; always re-verify against a primary source before trusting a catalyst date

entryStrategy.verdict: Measured median at-catalyst return across the core lane is -6.9% (n=54) — buying at today's $7.56 is not the default entry; the $6.40-6.80 zone is preferred. This is a corrected thesis, not a broken one: the specific catalyst this pick was built on (NAVSUNLI resubmission) is void near-term, but RGX-202's Phase III win and this-quarter BLA guidance is a real, still-intact near-term catalyst that analysts have largely kept faith in post-setback.
